service.description: What needs an administrator on this instance, as one list (plans/Tools-Fancy.md §3.4). Each item is {key, severity (critical, warning or info), text, count, value, link, parameters}: count for an item that counts records (at most 100: a count of 100 is "100 or more"), value for a resource reading (its percent), link a route under /apps with its parameters. The resource readings whose level is not ok come first (the status map's Resources: disk space and inodes of each filesystem, memory, CPU load, open files, the certificates the HTTPS listener serves, swap), the most severe first; then the listeners and integrations that failed or were skipped, a draining instance, saturated workers or database pool, a silent cluster member, failed job runs of the last 24 hours, an embedded database with no scheduled backup, system messages in error, open incidents, firing alerts, failing checks and scrape targets, new error groups, lost telemetry and agent approvals waiting. Each item is checked on its own: one that fails is logged as an error and left out, and the others still come back. An item whose source the user may not read (the entity, the dataset, the service, or MONITOR_INCIDENT for incidents) is left out; it reads nothing but counts. Refuses nothing.

parameter.name: items
parameter.description: The items, resource readings first, then the most severe first

service.description: The recent history of the System home's counters, for their sparklines: for each of load, memory, disk, workers and pool the values of its gauge over the period (from, such as now-1h), one a bucket of the range, oldest first, null where there is none; disk is the fullest filesystem's in each bucket. Read from the otel_metrics dataset through the report engine as the user, narrowed to instanceId when one is given. A series that cannot be read (telemetry off, the dataset not the user's to read, a query that fails) is logged, when it is a failure, and left out; the others still come back. Refuses nothing.

parameter.name: series
parameter.description: load, memory, disk, workers, pool: each a list of numbers
